freePlan.limits: No dedicated free plan, but small free allowances are included: community support, first 10 single-hostname SSL certificates per org, first 10GB of volume snapshot storage per month, shared IPv4 and unlimited Anycast IPv6.

keyLimits.en: No base subscription fee; per-organization usage billing, pro-rated by provisioning time. Shared-CPU Machines from about $0.00000078 to $0.00003429 per second depending on cores/RAM; Performance-CPU Machines from about $0.00001242 to $0.00019556 per second; stopped Machines billed at $0.15/GB rootfs per month. Volumes $0.15/GB per month; volume snapshots $0.08/GB per month (first 10GB free); dedicated IPv4 $2/month; data egress $0.02-$0.12/GB depending on region.

addOns.en: Reservation discounts of about 40% on committed compute blocks (roughly $36 to $14,400/year).
Fly Kubernetes at a $75/month base plus compute costs.

cautions.en: Pure usage-based billing with no flat subscription tier: total monthly cost depends on how many Machines run, for how long, and how much storage/egress is used, making it hard to predict without modeling actual traffic.
A credit card is required for most organizations even to start using paid resources beyond the small included allowances.

capabilities.en: Deploys containerized applications as 'Fly Machines' (VMs) across a global network of regions, close to end users.
Managed Postgres, Fly Volumes for persistent storage, and third-party extensions such as Tigris and Upstash Redis.
Fly Kubernetes for teams that want a managed Kubernetes control plane on top of Fly's infrastructure.

limitations.en: No flat, predictable subscription plan; billing is fully usage-based per organization.
Managed Postgres instances exist outside of regular apps, so deleting an app does not automatically delete its associated database, a common source of surprise cost.

reason.en: Comparable PaaS for deploying containerized/web apps quickly, with a more classic dyno-based pricing model versus Fly's usage-based Machines.
Overlaps for deploying containerized apps and managed infrastructure at usage-based or flat-rate pricing.
Common alternative for deploying web apps/serverless functions, though more frontend-framework-focused than Fly's general container hosting.

missingAlternatives.name: Railway
missingAlternatives.reason: Frequently cited direct competitor to Fly.io for deploying containerized apps with usage-based pricing; not present in the catalogue.

unknowns: Full per-service rate card (every storage/network/Postgres tier) was not exhaustively captured; only the rates surfaced on the pricing overview page were recorded.
Whether any legacy free-tier allowance for compute hours still applies (Fly.io removed a broader free tier in the past) was not explicitly reconfirmed beyond the small allowances listed.
